item.title: Hurricane Trudy reaches Category 3 strength off Mexico’s Pacific coast
item.dc:creator: Sara Pimentel
item.description: Hurricane Trudy strengthened into a Category 3 major hurricane on Friday and is expected to approach Mexico’s Pacific coast this weekend, with forecasters warning of dangerous rainfall, flooding and landslides. According to […]
item.content:encoded:
Hurricane Trudy strengthened into a Category 3 major hurricane on Friday and is expected to approach Mexico’s Pacific coast this weekend, with forecasters warning of dangerous rainfall, flooding and landslides.

According to the U.S. National Hurricane Center (NHC), Trudy had maximum sustained winds of 120 mph (195 km/h) and was moving north-northwest at about 5 mph (8 km/h). As of Friday morning, its center was approximately 235 miles (380 kilometers) southwest of Acapulco and 325 miles (525 kilometers) south-southeast of Manzanillo.

The hurricane had a minimum central pressure of 956 millibars. The NHC said additional strengthening was expected through Saturday, with Trudy forecast to remain a major hurricane as it makes its closest approach to Mexico.

A hurricane warning is in effect for portions of Mexico’s Pacific coast, while authorities are closely monitoring the storm as it moves toward the southwestern and west-central coast.

The latest forecast indicates that Trudy could pass very close to the coast late Saturday. Reuters reported that the storm could come within roughly 60 to 65 kilometers of the coasts of Jalisco and Colima, although a direct landfall was not currently expected.

item.title: Dominican government vows to continue defending rice production against U.S. interests
item.dc:creator: Sara Pimentel
item.description: Santo Domingo.- Vice President Raquel Peña led a presentation on the latest advances in rice production in the Dominican Republic, highlighting the sector’s growth over the past two decades, the development of […]
item.content:encoded:
Santo Domingo.- Vice President Raquel Peña led a presentation on the latest advances in rice production in the Dominican Republic, highlighting the sector’s growth over the past two decades, the development of new varieties and efforts to improve productivity, profitability and sustainability.

According to data presented during the event, national white rice production increased from approximately 9.2 million quintals in 2005 to nearly 14.8 million in 2025. Productivity reached 5,477.75 kilograms of paddy rice per hectare in 2025.

Among the advances highlighted were the LRC JUMA 69-20 and LRC JUMA 70-22 varieties, as well as the potential of JUMA 71-25, which is tolerant to certain herbicides and could help improve weed control and reduce production costs.

Government measures to strengthen rice production

Minister of the Presidency Andrés Bautista García highlighted government measures to support rice producers, including subsidies for certified seeds and fertilizers, preferential financing through the Agricultural Bank, agricultural insurance, irrigation and drainage maintenance, and pledging programs.

He also outlined a multi-year plan for the rice sector that includes creating a specialized fund, expanding financing and seed certification, promoting agricultural research, and improving irrigation, drainage and rural roads.

The government also plans to review rice marketing mechanisms to promote greater transparency in weighing, tare and moisture requirements, with particular attention to small and medium-sized producers.

Bautista emphasized the importance of cooperation among government institutions, farmers, researchers and the private sector to promote innovation and technology in rice production.

He said maintaining the progress achieved in the sector will require greater access to technology and improved conditions for farmers, stressing that protecting domestic rice production is essential to food security, the rural economy and the livelihoods of thousands of Dominican families.

item.title: Dominican Republic orders extradition of three citizens to the United States
item.dc:creator: Sara Pimentel
item.description: Santo Domingo.- Dominican Vice President Raquel Peña, acting as head of the Executive Branch, ordered the extradition of three Dominican citizens to the United States through Decrees 716-26, 717-26 and 718-26. The […]
item.content:encoded:
Santo Domingo.- Dominican Vice President Raquel Peña, acting as head of the Executive Branch, ordered the extradition of three Dominican citizens to the United States through Decrees 716-26, 717-26 and 718-26.

The orders involve Darío Bautista, Ramón Joaquín Romero Bastardo and Luis Arismendy Paca Méndez, who are wanted in separate cases in the United States.

Bautista is wanted under an indictment filed in August 2025 in the U.S. District Court for the District of Puerto Rico. He is accused of conspiring to import five kilograms or more of cocaine into the United States.

Romero Bastardo is wanted in connection with a case filed in October 2024 in the Supreme Court of New York, Bronx County. He faces charges including second-degree murder, first-degree manslaughter, first-degree gang assault, second-degree assault and fourth-degree unlawful possession of a weapon.

Paca Méndez is wanted under a superseding indictment filed in February 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York. He is accused of conspiracy to commit wire fraud.

The three extradition orders were issued while Peña was serving as acting head of the Executive Branch.

item.title: Veterans’ Brotherhood president meets with Dominicans in New York
item.dc:creator: Sara Pimentel
item.description: New York.- The Brotherhood of Retired Veterans of the Armed Forces and the National Police conducted an institutional mission to Rhode Island and Massachusetts from October 11 to 14, meeting with government […]
item.content:encoded:
New York.- The Brotherhood of Retired Veterans of the Armed Forces and the National Police conducted an institutional mission to Rhode Island and Massachusetts from October 11 to 14, meeting with government officials, community organizations and institutions that support veterans.

The delegation was led by retired Major General Valerio García Reyes, president of the Brotherhood, along with his wife, Dr. Adaía Rosario, and Dr. Luis Díaz Martínez, a Vietnam veteran and president of the Griffin Foundation.

The four-day visit included 17 activities and resulted in seven recognitions from state and municipal authorities, including Rhode Island Senator Ana Quezada, Lieutenant Governor Sabina Matos, the mayor of Providence and members of the City Council.

The delegation also visited the Providence VA Medical Center and Rhode Island Community Food Bank and held meetings with law enforcement officials and community organizations.

In Lawrence, Massachusetts, the group met with Dr. José Báez and toured Primary Quality Health Care to learn about its primary care model and explore potential cooperation in healthcare.

One of the key meetings was held at Home Base in Boston, where Chief Operating Officer Michael D. Allard presented programs focused on mental health, rehabilitation and comprehensive support for veterans.

The Brotherhood invited Home Base representatives to visit the Dominican Republic and proposed exploring a memorandum of understanding to develop support initiatives for Dominican and U.S. veterans living in the country.

According to the Brotherhood, the meetings also identified potential areas of cooperation in healthcare, food security, community programs and technology. Any agreements resulting from the discussions would be formalized at a later stage.

item.title: Bisonó proposes five areas to strengthen US-Caribbean cooperation
item.dc:creator: Sara Pimentel
item.description: Washington, DC.- Foreign Minister Víctor “Ito” Bisonó presented five areas of action to strengthen cooperation between the United States and Caribbean countries during the opening of the U.S.-Caribbean Dialogue on Thursday at […]
item.content:encoded:
Washington, DC.- Foreign Minister Víctor “Ito” Bisonó presented five areas of action to strengthen cooperation between the United States and Caribbean countries during the opening of the U.S.-Caribbean Dialogue on Thursday at the U.S. State Department in Washington.

Bisonó proposed promoting regional energy security projects, turning economic diplomacy into new investments and productive partnerships, protecting strategic infrastructure through cybersecurity, cargo traceability and port security, strengthening joint responses to natural disasters and health emergencies, and intensifying efforts against drug trafficking, narco-terrorism, transnational crime and illicit arms trafficking.

The dialogue, convened by the U.S. State Department, brought together Caribbean government representatives and U.S. officials to discuss security, energy, economic growth and strategic infrastructure. Bisonó attended alongside Dominican Defense Minister Lieutenant General Carlos Antonio Fernández Onofre and Dominican Ambassador to the United States María Isabel Castillo.

Bisonó’s participation is part of an official visit to Washington from October 14 to 17, which also includes meetings with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Organization of American States Secretary General Albert Ramdin.

item.title: Breeze Airways announces new nonstop flights from Tampa to Santo Domingo
item.dc:creator: Sara Pimentel
item.description: Breeze Airways will launch nonstop flights between Tampa and Santo Domingo in June 2027, adding a new year-round air service between Florida and the Dominican Republic. The new Tampa-Santo Domingo route will […]
item.content:encoded:
Breeze Airways will launch nonstop flights between Tampa and Santo Domingo in June 2027, adding a new year-round air service between Florida and the Dominican Republic.

The new Tampa-Santo Domingo route will begin operating on June 18, 2027, with two weekly flights on Mondays and Fridays between Tampa International Airport (TPA) and Las Américas International Airport (AILA). The airline will operate the service with Airbus A220-300 aircraft.

Flights will depart Tampa at 10:30 a.m. and arrive in Santo Domingo at 1:25 p.m. Return flights will leave Santo Domingo at 2:25 p.m. and arrive in Tampa at 5:30 p.m. All times are local.

According to Tampa International Airport, Breeze’s new service will mark the first year-round airline service between Tampa and Santo Domingo. Santo Domingo will become Breeze’s sixth international destination from Tampa and its second destination in the Dominican Republic, after Punta Cana.

The new route will increase competition in the Tampa-Santo Domingo market. Frontier Airlines is scheduled to launch its own nonstop service between the two cities on December 17, 2026.

item.title: Dominican Republic promotes tourism in Houston with roadshow
item.dc:creator: Sara Pimentel
item.description: Houston, Texas.- Tourism Minister David Collado led the Dominican Republic’s 124th international tourism roadshow on Thursday in Houston, Texas, where he met with more than 200 travel agents, tour operators, airline representatives […]
item.content:encoded:
Houston, Texas.- Tourism Minister David Collado led the Dominican Republic’s 124th international tourism roadshow on Thursday in Houston, Texas, where he met with more than 200 travel agents, tour operators, airline representatives and other tourism industry stakeholders.

Collado presented the country’s tourism offerings and highlighted Houston as a strategic market with strong growth potential and connectivity to the Dominican Republic.

“We are here with you presenting not just a destination, but an unforgettable experience,” Collado said.

He noted that Houston ranks fifth among the Dominican Republic’s priority markets in its international tourism promotion strategy, underscoring the importance of strengthening the country’s presence in the city.

During the event, Collado also held meetings with tourism industry representatives to strengthen commercial ties, expand business opportunities and promote the Dominican Republic as both a vacation and investment destination.

Travel agents remain a key part of the strategy. The Ministry of Tourism has more than 35,000 agents registered on its DO Travel Rewards platform, which provides information on the country’s tourism offerings and encourages their promotion in international markets.

The Houston event is part of the ministry’s efforts to strengthen the Dominican Republic’s international tourism position, diversify source markets and expand opportunities for continued sector growth.

item.title: Health Ministry urges Dominicans to strengthen dengue prevention measures
item.dc:creator: Sara Pimentel
item.description: Santo Domingo.- The Ministry of Public Health urged Dominicans to strengthen dengue prevention by eliminating mosquito breeding sites, properly managing stored water and seeking medical attention promptly if symptoms appear. Health Minister […]
item.content:encoded:
Santo Domingo.- The Ministry of Public Health urged Dominicans to strengthen dengue prevention by eliminating mosquito breeding sites, properly managing stored water and seeking medical attention promptly if symptoms appear.

Health Minister Víctor Atallah emphasized the need for continued prevention at homes and in communities, despite favorable national indicators, as weather conditions could increase the risk of dengue transmission.

As of epidemiological week 39 of 2026, the Dominican Republic had recorded 396 confirmed dengue cases, including about 15 reported during the week. Authorities said cases remain within the favorable zone of the endemic corridor and below the expected threshold based on the 2019–2025 historical pattern.

The ministry also reported the circulation of the DENV-2 dengue serotype and urged residents to avoid self-medication and seek care for symptoms such as high fever. Although the national trend remains favorable, localized increases could occur.

The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) has reported nearly 1.7 million suspected dengue cases in the Americas through epidemiological week 36. Authorities warned that weather conditions associated with El Niño could favor the reproduction of the Aedes aegypti mosquito, making continued surveillance and prevention essential.

Families are advised to keep tanks, cisterns and other water containers tightly covered; empty, scrub and clean containers weekly; remove standing water from tires, bottles, cans and flowerpots; and inspect patios, roofs and gutters after rainfall.

People who suspect they have dengue should avoid aspirin and ibuprofen because of the risk of bleeding. Paracetamol (acetaminophen) may be used for fever or pain as directed by a healthcare professional.

item.title: Abinader announces plans for Dominican House of Culture in Italy
item.dc:creator: Sara Pimentel
item.description: Rome, Italy.- President Luis Abinader announced that the Dominican Republic will allocate funds starting in January 2027 to support the creation of a Dominican House of Culture in Italy, aimed at promoting […]
item.content:encoded:
Rome, Italy.- President Luis Abinader announced that the Dominican Republic will allocate funds starting in January 2027 to support the creation of a Dominican House of Culture in Italy, aimed at promoting Dominican traditions and strengthening ties with the diaspora.

The announcement was made during a meeting with Dominican community representatives in Italy, attended by First Lady Raquel Arbaje. Abinader said the Presidency will provide a donation to cover the rental and operation of a space, while Dominican Ambassador to Italy Rafael Antonio Lantigua will coordinate the preparatory work with community representatives, including the selection of the location.

The cultural center is expected to promote Dominican art, traditions and customs, particularly among children and young people born or raised in Italy. Diaspora representatives proposed activities including folkloric groups, carnival costume and instrument workshops, summer camps, and programs focused on Dominican history and national symbols.

They also called for greater support for entrepreneurs, improved opportunities for Dominican professionals through academic degree recognition, and assistance with pensions, employment and communication with Dominican authorities.

Abinader said his administration would evaluate the proposals and highlighted the role of the Institute of Dominicans Abroad (INDEX) in supporting Dominicans living overseas.

The president also recognized the diaspora’s contribution to the Dominican economy through remittances, which he said support consumption, construction and the country’s balance of payments. He noted that the Dominican Republic expects to receive about 12.5 million visitors in 2026 and highlighted progress in reducing poverty and undernourishment.

Ambassador Lantigua praised Abinader’s engagement with the Dominican diaspora, particularly his interest in issues involving education, employment and driver’s licenses. He said the meeting provided an opportunity to strengthen ties between the government and Dominicans in Italy while promoting Dominican culture and identity abroad.

item.title: More than 5,000 tourism jobs offered at employment fair in La Romana
item.dc:creator: Sara Pimentel
item.description: La Romana.- More than 5,000 job opportunities were offered to Dominicans during the “Your Job Is Here: in Tourism” employment fair organized by the Ministry of Labor in La Romana, with participation […]
item.content:encoded:
La Romana.- More than 5,000 job opportunities were offered to Dominicans during the “Your Job Is Here: in Tourism” employment fair organized by the Ministry of Labor in La Romana, with participation from more than 50 tourism companies.

The event, held at the Eleoncio Mercedes Sports Center, brought together employers and job seekers as part of efforts to address the tourism sector’s hiring needs and facilitate access to formal employment.

Juan Bancalari, president of the Dominican Hotel and Tourism Association (Asonahores), described tourism as the country’s main source of income and encouraged Dominicans to pursue technical and professional training to meet the sector’s growing demand for skilled workers.

The participation of more than 50 companies strengthened public-private cooperation by allowing applicants to present their professional profiles and connect directly with employers through recruitment processes.

During the event, the Ministry of Labor also recognized Bancalari for his contribution to tourism development and job creation, while Rafael Blanco Canto was honored for his career and contributions to strengthening the industry.

The ministry said the initiative forms part of its efforts to strengthen employment intermediation services, bring job opportunities closer to the population and support the incorporation of more workers into the formal labor market.
